purpose: Real upstream wire output used to cross-check internal/adapters/queryinput decoders (02.08-W5). Black-box: no upstream code is linked or copied.

remote_write.sender: Prometheus 3.13.5 (image soundpost-oracle-promql-prometheus-3.13.5:latest, binary /bin/prometheus via --entrypoint; lock id promql-prometheus-3.13.5, mirror.gcr.io/prom/prometheus@sha256:dc30314819e04a1a3d18d0b37eaa9c8e4e18f33f026e3e2d81bf127c7cddcd55)
remote_write.how: docker network sp-w4cap; python:3.13-slim container running cap.py (serves fixture-exposition.om as OpenMetrics and stores each POST /write/v1|v2 body); Prometheus run with prom.yml and --enable-feature=exemplar-storage,native-histograms,metadata-wal-records, scrape_interval 1s, two remote_write blocks (v1 and v2 'io.prometheus.write.v2.Request'). Bodies stored verbatim (snappy block, golang/snappy); headers as received in *.headers.json.
remote_write.files: rw-v1-NNN.bin, rw-v2-NNN.bin, rw-*.headers.json, prom.yml, cap.py, fixture-exposition.om (the scraped input)
remote_write.notes: Prometheus drops native custom-bucket histograms for v1 (queue_manager warning), so the histogram appears in v2 only. The v2 response lacked X-Prometheus-Remote-Write-*-Written headers so Prometheus logged non-recoverable errors; the request bodies were still captured and are unaffected. rw-v1-001.headers.json is absent: the capture server's header file for the first request did not survive the docker cp; the body is intact.
